title: Spring Framework Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Create a managed value
examples.description: @Bean marks a value that Spring creates. The context is a container that lets the program find that value.

examples.title: Find a bean by name
examples.description: The method name becomes the bean name. This example asks for the bean called school.

examples.title: Choose between two values
examples.description: A container can hold several beans of one type. A name selects the one you need.

examples.title: Connect two objects
examples.description: Spring can pass one bean into another bean method. This is dependency injection: the object receives what it needs.

examples.title: Share one bean instance
examples.description: The normal Spring scope is singleton: one instance per bean definition in the container.

examples.title: Ask for a fresh instance
examples.description: Prototype scope makes a new bean each time the container is asked for it.

examples.title: Create a bean when needed
examples.description: @Lazy delays this bean until it is requested. The print inside its factory shows when creation happens.

examples.title: Read a configured value
examples.description: @Value can read a property with a fallback. No lesson.score property is set, so the fallback is 8.

examples.title: Run a setup method
examples.description: initMethod names a method Spring calls after making the bean.

examples.title: Run cleanup when closing
examples.description: destroyMethod names cleanup. Closing the context runs it for this singleton bean.

examples.title: Choose a default bean
examples.description: @Primary marks the preferred bean when several beans match a type.

examples.title: Check whether a bean exists
examples.description: containsBean lets code check a registered name before trying to read it.
